# Fixture provenance: tds_payees vouchers that share a GUID (#1243)

Every book here is invented, with round figures and plain names: no fixture is a Tally read of any real assessee.

## What these fixtures establish, and what they do not

The reference changed, at its commit `49c33c71`, how `tds_payees` keys the vouchers of a payee row. Before it, a row kept each voucher's credit, date and voucher by GUID alone, so two vouchers sharing a GUID (a blank GUID, or one GUID repeated) became one bill: their amounts summed into one credit dated by the later voucher, in the single-sum test, the month totals, the largest single bill, the TDS seen on a payee's vouchers, the tranches clause 21(b) lists and the reversals the client's list classifies. Now each voucher of the population has a key no other shares (its GUID where that is unique, so nothing that reads it moves, else the GUID and its place among those sharing it); a citation still names a voucher by its GUID and label, and the client's list of reversals still names a voucher, and a bill, by GUID, so a classification reads on every voucher holding it. The 135 goldens pinned then regenerated byte-identical at `49c33c71` (checked 6 Oct 2026).

- `edge-books/tds_payees_shared_guid_bills.json`: two blank-GUID bills, and one GUID on two bills, under the single sum and the aggregate (no finding); five blank-GUID bills crossing the aggregate (the largest single bill is one bill, each is cited and each is its own clause 21(b) row); four blank-GUID bills of one day on a goods-carriage ledger, two with one number (one cited ref), whose labels sort apart from the books' order, which their keys follow (the s.194C(6) question; each bill is a clause 21(b) row, numbered in key order); rent in two months each under the limit, and a month whose total counts each blank-GUID credit in its own month; one GUID on three bills of one day, two with identical refs; two bills of one day each over the single sum, a unique GUID read before a blank one, numbered in key order (the blank GUID's first), not the books'. 61 figures, 6 findings.
- `edge-books/tds_payees_shared_guid_tds.json`: two blank-GUID journals each carrying TDS against a payee (both seen); three blank-GUID plain bills each carrying its own TDS: one deducted on its own voucher, two short of a rate in a month the challans show nothing deposited for (clause 21(b)(ii)(B) and the short-deduction finding); two blank-GUID bills whose TDS the books do not divide between two parties, each under the single sum with it. 58 figures, 6 findings.
- `edge-books/tds_payees_shared_guid_reversals.json`: two reversals sharing a GUID, and two blank-GUID reversals, classified as credit notes (both named); a bill-specific reversal naming a GUID two bills of the payee share (against either); eleven bills sharing a GUID named by a duplicate-or-error reversal (against each, in the books' order); one GUID on a bill to each of two payees, named by a reversal on one (against that payee's bill only); a listed reversal GUID no voucher holds. 76 figures, 7 findings.
- Not reached: a GUID holding a NUL that would make two keys equal, which the reference refuses (no read produces one); it is a unit test in `src/book.rs`, not a book. The reference's `taxable_tranches` (read by `tds_interest_201`, not ported) is not reached either.
- Regression fixtures only: they prove the port and the reference agree on the same book, and nothing about reading Tally. The evidence for real books is local parity on real reads, never committed.

## How they were produced

At the reference engine (a private repository), commit `ed9a29af8a4dec76baf3ea42c3425e9b0151e642` (6 Oct 2026), from an archive of its `tae/` only, under Python 3.13. Since `49c33c71` the reference zero-pads a key's place to eight digits (its commit `19617356`), so the keys of one GUID sort in the books' order: in `tds_payees_shared_guid_bills` the four Carrier G bills (the eighth to eleventh blank GUIDs) take their clause 21(b) row numbers in that order, where an unpadded place put the tenth and eleventh first. That moves only which voucher each of the four `194C_row_21b_a` rows of Carrier G cites; no value moves. Since every voucher of one GUID now keys in the books' order, the book also holds Carrier K (two bills of one day with different GUIDs, read against their key order), so the key order of a day's bills is still told apart from the books'; that adds five figures and one finding. The other two goldens are byte-identical to `49c33c71`'s, and every `tds_payees` golden already committed (twenty edge books and the synthetic read) regenerates byte-identical at `ed9a29af`. At `49c33c71`'s parent each of the three new goldens differs. The invocation:

    uv run -q --python 3.13 --with openpyxl --with xlrd --with python-docx --with jsonschema \
        --with striprtf --with pdfplumber python parity/edge_golden.py ENGINE \
        tests/fixtures/edge-books/NAME.json tests/fixtures/golden

The three books are written as data by a small generator, every voucher balancing; they are hand-chosen scenarios, not generated from any data.
